definition: Equinox is a small JAX library that represents neural networks as callable PyTrees, keeping everything plain JAX.

explainer.lead: How to install Equinox, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.inAi: Popular in scientific ML (neural ODEs, physics models) where you want full control of JAX transformations.
explainer.jsNote: Equinox is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is like a thin wrapper that lets you treat a model as an ordinary Python object while still using all your usual tools on it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to write modules that work directly with JAX's grad, jit and vmap; the pitfall is that it is deliberately minimal, so you assemble much yourself.
tiers.paperLevel: A small JAX library representing neural networks as callable PyTrees; created by Patrick Kidger in 2021. Limits: scope is intentionally small, leaving ecosystem features to other tools.

explainer.example: A linear layer is defined as a callable PyTree; jax.grad and jax.jit apply to it directly with no extra wrappers.
